create.name: Langri Tangpa Centre
create.bio:
Langri Tangpa Centre is a Tibetan Buddhist teaching and meditation centre in Camp Hill, on Brisbane's southside, affiliated with the FPMT. It grew from a small city group that Inta Mckimm, a Latvian-born student of Lama Zopa Rinpoche, ran from her own lounge room from 1982; Rinpoche later renamed it after Langri Tangpa, whose Eight Verses for Training the Mind the centre holds dear. Her daughter Miffi Maxmillion took over its running, and in 2007 the community bought its present building with a meditation hall, library and life-size Buddha.

Volunteers run the centre and every class is by donation. Senior students lead Sunday guided meditations for beginners, Eddie Peet has taught FPMT's three-year Discovering Buddhism course there for many years, and resident nuns lead pujas, sutra recitations and short courses. Visiting geshes and FPMT teachers add retreats and seasonal teachings. Much of the programme runs both in the hall and on Zoom, and its YouTube channel offers practice-along recordings of pujas, mandala offering and purification meditations.

courses.title: Core Program – Discovering Buddhism
courses.description: FPMT's fourteen-module foundation course, run here over about three years with weekly classes on Tuesday mornings or Wednesday evenings, in the hall or online. Each module covers one theme, from the mind's potential to emptiness and tantra, followed by review and practice.

courses.title: Meditation: Calm, Cleanse & Inspire
courses.description: A Sunday morning session for newcomers and regulars, led by senior students: a breathing meditation, an open question time, then a guided Buddha visualisation with mantra, followed by chai.
courses.price: All our classes are by donation

free_resources.title: Discovering Buddhism Videos & First Classes
free_resources.description: Short FPMT films for each Discovering Buddhism module, plus recordings of the opening class of each module as taught at the centre, free to watch before joining.
